content: Interlanguage links are hyperlinks that connect a page in one language version of Wikipedia to the equivalent page in another language version. These links are also used across other Wikimedia projects, such as Wiktionary, Wikisource, Wikiquote, and Wikibooks. On Wikimedia Commons, interlanguage links provide connections to Wikipedia pages, but the reverse is not true; links from Wikipedia to Commons are treated as standard in-page links. These links are typically displayed on the edges of a webpage, depending on the interface being used (e.g., on the left in Monobook or at the top and bottom in Classic). They are labeled under Other languages and display the names of the available languages. While they may resemble external links in appearance, their syntax is more similar to internal links. For further details, refer to the Meta page on interlanguage links. The syntax for interlanguage links involves using a two-letter language code as defined by ISO 639-1. For example, en represents English, and de represents German. In an article like Plankton, which exists in multiple languages, the interlanguage links are formatted to appear in a special sidebar section labeled in other languages. These links are not displayed within the body of the text. Previously, they were placed at the top of the page, but this caused issues such as excessive whitespace, confusion for new editors, and interference with search results. As a result, interlanguage links are now required to be placed in the sidebar. Their placement in the article's source code does not affect their visual appearance on the rendered page, except for the order in which they are displayed. It is important not to include a link to the language in which the article is written. In the past, the Chinese Wikipedia maintained separate versions of articles in Simplified and Traditional Chinese scripts. However, script conversion is now automated, eliminating the need for separate links for these versions. For other languages, there are lists of pages where interlanguage links may be needed. For instance, an English article might link to a Spanish article, but the corresponding Spanish article might lack a link back to the English version. Examples of such lists include pages for Dutch, Esperanto, French, German, Polish, and Spanish interlanguage links. For more information on collaborating across language versions of Wikipedia, refer to resources like Wikipedia:Embassy and Wikipedia:Multilingual coordination. If you contribute to Wikipedia in multiple languages, it is helpful to monitor new pages in those languages and check for corresponding articles in English. This allows you to add interlanguage links in both directions. Ordinary interlanguage links are designed to connect corresponding pages in different languages. However, if a topic does not yet have a page in English but exists in another language, it can be useful to create an inline interlanguage link. For example, the English article Movie theaters in the Netherlands might include an inline link to the Dutch article nl:Tuschinski Theater if the English version of that article does not yet exist. This approach encourages users to write or translate the missing article. Once the article is created, the interlanguage link can be replaced with a standard internal link. Inline interlanguage links should only be used when the topic is relevant to the language being linked. For instance, it would be appropriate to link Sigmund Freud to the German Wikipedia if the English article did not exist, but it would not be appropriate to link to a page about light bulbs in another language if the topic is unrelated. To create an inline interlanguage link, you can add a colon before the language abbreviation. For example, :fr:Littérature française au XVIIIe siècle would create a clickable link to the French article on 18th-century French literature. You can also use a pipe to display only the title of the linked page. Inline interlanguage links can be used in talk pages and on Meta, where they appear as regular links. In normal articles, the method described above should be used to link to non-corresponding articles in other languages. The syntax for interlanguage links differs slightly from that used for interwiki links, which connect pages across different Wikimedia projects. For example, the prefix :en can be used to link directly to the English Wikipedia, while MetaWikiPedia (or m) can be used to link to Meta. For more information on interwiki links, see Wikipedia:Sister projects and the list of language codes. Links to pages on other wikis, including other Wikimedia Foundation sites, are displayed differently from internal links within the English Wikipedia. These links do not indicate whether the target page exists. If the target page does not exist, clicking the link will lead to a blank page. This indicates that the article has not yet been written in the target language. Blank interlanguage links on the English Wikipedia may be deleted or commented out. It is recommended to create at least a stub article before adding interlanguage links to it. This allows others to expand the content by translating it from the original language. New articles should be sorted alphabetically based on the local language, as described in the Meta page on interwiki sorting order. Most articles currently follow this method. Sorting alphabetically by the two-letter language codes is also acceptable. While other sorting methods exist, consistency across articles is encouraged. In certain cases, you may need to use the regular external link syntax instead of interlanguage links. This applies when linking from languages that do not yet support the interlanguage link feature or when specifying additional text in the link to clarify differences between the subjects of the articles.
